title: Refine rollback automation and analyze shadow traffic gaps after canary failure
creator: Marcus Li
summary: Follow-up work from a failed canary rollout where the model variant increased tail latency and produced a spike in low-confidence hallucinations. The automatic rollback did not trigger reliably; shadow traffic was not enabled for the rollout path. This ticket consolidates runbook fixes, safety checks, monitoring improvements, and rollout policy changes to prevent recurrence.
incident_timeline: 2026-02-20: Canary roll started (10% traffic). 2026-02-20 12:15: sudden rise in 95p and 99p latency for affected route. 2026-02-20 12:20: Increase in rejected/generated low-confidence answers detected by quality eval webhook. 2026-02-20 12:23: Auto-rollback attempted but failed to reduce traffic due to mis-evaluated health probe (probe used token-count not time). 2026-02-20 12:37: Manual rollback executed; traffic returned to baseline. 2026-02-20 13:05: Post-rollback validation showed no residual error rates.
root_cause: Primary cause: model variant used a new quantized kernel on the serving runtime that regressed tail latency for long-context requests. Secondary cause: health probe for auto-rollback was measuring token throughput instead of latency and quality signals; thresholds were too permissive. Tertiary cause: rollout path had shadow traffic disabled so we lacked pre-rollback quality evidence and missed early low-confidence signal aggregation.
detection_signals: Spikes in 95p/99p latency from Prometheus (p99 +230ms), quality webhook sent increased low-confidence flag rate (+14%), user-facing error rate remained low but human QA surfaced degraded answer quality for long prompts. Alerting was triggered by latency threshold only; no combined latency+quality composite alert existed.
immediate_mitigation: Manual rollback executed and traffic shifted to baseline model. Short-term config change: lowered canary traffic to 2% for future immediate retries until safer checks in place. Added temporary alert rule to correlate low-confidence webhook with latency spikes.
runbook_changes:
- Add preflight checklist that mandates a shadowing step (1 hour at 10% shadow) for any model with new kernel/quantization.
- Update health probe definition to include a composite metric: sliding-window of p95 latency + low-confidence webhook rate.
- Document manual rollback playbook with exact CLI commands, expected timing, and verification queries (promql examples included).
- Add owner escalation matrix and Slack escalation channel for canary rollouts.
rollout_policy_changes:
- Require shadow traffic enabled by default for all model version rollouts where runtime kernel or quantization profile changes.
- Reduce default canary step sizes and increase observation windows for long-context models.
- Add automatic preflight offline eval step that runs a standardized prompt set with latency and quality thresholds before production canarying.
monitoring_checks:
- New dashboards: Canary Composite Health (p95 latency, low-confidence rate, error rate).
- Alerts: CanaryHealthComposite > threshold for 5m -> PagerDuty P0.
- Synthetic traffic job: daily synthetic long-context run against candidate models to detect regressions before canary.
- Shadow aggregator: consolidate shadow request outputs and run quality evals in near-real time.

acceptance_criteria:
- Composite health probe is used for auto-rollback and tested in staging.
- Shadowing is enabled by default; at least one successful shadow run completed for candidate model.
- Synthetic long-context job reports detectable regression for baseline change in controlled test.
- Runbook updated and reviewed by SRE and runtime leads.
- New alerts are firing in canary regression test and PagerDuty escalation validated.
notes: We intentionally keep the synthetic long-context suite lightweight to run daily in a serverless job; if it becomes noisy we'll move it to weekly but keep shadow aggregation mandatory for runtime-level changes. Expect follow-up PRs to split the rollout controller and policy config to support per-team overrides.
